answer:
A seat is one log mark landed at a licensed wharf berth. The applicant files a timber mark from the forestry register, a berth number and a bond; the node refuses a mark or berth already seated, and a dormant berth shows an empty tally.

Fifty clones need fifty marks, berths and bonds: 750 dollars a year per mark, 2,400 for a scaling licence, 15,000 bond, 6,800 lease, near 1.25 million before a board is cut. After a gale the inspector reissues berth numbers, so an untended berth loses its seat.

A gale flattens every stack on the quay alike; the tally book separates whose timber is whose.
